utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I invite the Prosecution to call its next witness, I'd just like to put on the record that in an e-mail, VWS has announced that the result of the measurement of Witness 68 [sic] was 1 metre, 58 centimetres. Is that a measurement the parties could agree upon? Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: As far as I'm concerned, the answer to that would be yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, Mr. Emmerson? I see two times nodding yes, which I understand to be an affirmation. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I have every faith in the abilities of VWS to measure the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And I take it that this is also an acceptance of that fact and not an acceptance of the fact that they are able to do it. Yes, thank you. That's well understood. Then, Mr. Di Fazio, the next witness, no protective measures have been applied for, as far as I can see, although in the 2006 statement one would perhaps expect such a thing -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes, but that's -- that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but it's not. MR. DI FAZIO: There's just one very, very brief matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: I propose to tender his 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And there are some references in the last few paragraphs, in particular paragraphs 29 through to the end of the statement, that deal with some documents that should be kept confidential.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And I wonder how you would like me to proceed? I have got two versions of that 92 ter statement; one that fully includes -- that includes all those paragraphs; and another one that has those paragraphs blacked-out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll say one for -- MR. DI FAZIO: For the public --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the public. MR. DI FAZIO: -- consumption, and one under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: And if we deal with it that way, I think that just deals with the issue neatly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have they both already been uploaded into the system, or not yet? MR. DI FAZIO: I'm told they're both available, ready to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, do the two, the public and the non-public version of a document, do they get the same number with some annex, or is it two subsequent numbers? Yes. Then perhaps you already assign to the 92 ter statement, the non-public version, which number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number 270, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the public version would then be 271, marked for identification, not under seal. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see on the transcript I might have misspoken that Witness 68 was 1 metre 58, but it's Witness 61 that has been measured, just for correction of the transcript. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I simply say this, that there are expressions of opinion in the statement of this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- which go to ultimate questions that the Tribunal has to decide. They're not properly sourced. I don't imagine anybody would think twice about relying upon them, but they do, I think, find their way into the 92 ter statement. I'm looking at paragraph 35 of the consolidated witness statement, which I believe corresponds to paragraph 23 of the 92 ter statement. Yes. Those are not matters for, with the greatest of respect, they're not matters for a witness to give evidence about. Obviously, he can give evidence about what he saw, but -- MR. DI FAZIO: I have no quarrel with this, let's -- and I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: ECMM witnesses are not, with the greatest of respect, in a position to draw inferences about what connections could properly be made from what, by any definition, was partial information available to them. I simply raise it at this stage to put on the record the fact that whilst there's been no objection to the admission of a 92 ter statement containing that material, the proper admissibility of that material is a matter to be determined in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's agreed upon by Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it seems. Generally, may I make this observation, that if there is material in a witness statement which is plainly inadmissible, it ought not really to find its way into a 92 ter statement because the 92 ter statement is a form of admission of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, are you ready to -- MR. DI FAZIO: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that these observations are shared by the other counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Very much so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I understand your next witness will be Mr. Pappas. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you're ready to call him, I'll invite the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom. MR. DI FAZIO: The -- the summary I intend to read, and I don't see any problem with reading that in the presence of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, on the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, Mr. Pappas. Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. From your answer, I take it that you'll use the English language in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll do my best, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Before you give evidence, Mr. Pappas, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Pappas.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'll first be examined by Mr. Di Fazio, and I don't know whether Mr. Di Fazio explained already to you, but part of the evidence you give will be through a written statement, and Mr. Di Fazio will read a summary of that statement in order to inform the public what it is about. So it's not a summary that is your evidence. You'll later be asked about the statement itself, but this is just to inform the public and to make transparent what happens in this courtroom. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. A summary of the Rule 92 ter statement of Achilleas Pappas: "Achilleas Pappas is an officer in the Greek Air Force. In early January 1998, he was deployed with the European Commission Monitoring Mission in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In July 1998, he was transferred to Kosovo. He joined ECMM Team Pec I, based in Pec. He started to carry out his monitoring duties, which included monitoring Serb troop movements, meeting local community representatives, and obtaining information about the KLA. "The geographical extent of his work included the area up to the south of Djakovica municipality, north to the Montenegrin border, eastwards to the Klina municipality, and westwards to the Albanian border. "He observed that Serb forces controlled the main towns, such as Pec and Djakovica, and the main roads connecting these towns in western Kosovo. Serbian check-points existed along these main roads. "While looking for KLA check-points, he observed that check-points on the Pec-Djakovica road were manned by young men on that part of the road north of Decane. He encountered the same thing on the Pec-Pristina road. The young men manning these check-points did not claim to be members of the KLA. However, in the areas off the main Pec-Djakovica road south of Decane" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, would you please slow down? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that several booths are a bit behind. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, my apologies. "However, in the areas off the main Pec-Djakovica road south of Decane, he noted the presence of KLA check-points. "In villages in rural areas, he noted that the KLA received public support by local villagers, but in private conversations he noted an element of fear of the KLA amongst some villagers. He noted that the KLA occupied rural areas away from the main roads. However, he did on one occasion see a Serb tank and Serb soldiers looting and burning a village south of the Pec-Pristina road. "In carrying out his duties, he participated in the drafting of reports and became familiar with reports detailing the activities of his team. He can comment on a number of documents detailing the activities of ECMM monitors. "On 17 September 1998, he visited the local court in Pec and spoke to court officials. As a result, he attended a makeshift morgue in a hotel in Djakovica and the canal area near Lake Radonjic on 18 September 1998. He saw 24 body-bags at the morgue. After visiting the canal site, he went to a small nearby farm in company with Serb officials and saw cables alleged to have been used to tie-up victims and one which had what he thought was human hair still attached. He also saw a small training ground at the farm, and he noted targets for rifle practice with bullet-holes and other fixtures that seemed to be part of an obstacle course. "Mr. Pappas met with Ramush Haradinaj on one occasion on 11 August 1998. Oral evidence will be led of this encounter. He observed him to be a cool-headed individual who exercised tight control over his subordinates." That, if Your Honours please, is the summary of the Rule 92 ter evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry to rise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder if I might invite Mr. Di Fazio - and it may, I readily recognise, be entirely my misunderstanding - but I wonder if I might invite him to identify which paragraph in the 92 ter statement the first sentence and the second sentence of paragraph 3 in the summary that he has read are drawn from. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. That's -- sorry, just bear with me, Your Honours, I can -- I can find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What specifically? It comes close to 11, from what I -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, I'm just wondering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what portion exactly you had in mind, but -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, it is 11, it is 11. I'm sorry, for some reason, my copy's incomplete. I apologise for that. It is. It should be paragraph 11, that's -- that's -- that deals with it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, it may be my misunderstanding, but I don't understand paragraph 11 to indicate that there were check-points on the main roads manned by young men who were other than Serbs. So it doesn't seem to me, with respect, to reflect that paragraph at all. It seems to be referring to check-points in territory off the main road. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well -- well -- MR. DI FAZIO: Every day they drove off the main Pec-Djakovica road --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The first two sentences of paragraph 3 and, in fact, the first three sentences of paragraph 3, seem to be indicating that there were check-points by persons who were armed and who were obviously not Serbs on the main roads, and that does not seem to me to be a reflection of the statement at all. MR. DI FAZIO: Right. I'm sorry. I should -- perhaps it should be that the check-points were -- were off the main road -- my apologies, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It says -- the summary says: "On the main road." MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes. I agree. Perhaps if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The summary is not evidence, and it should read "off the main road." MR. DI FAZIO: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in the second sentence also, "off the main road." MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, "off the main road," that's right. That's right. Mr. Emmerson is quite right, and for the purposes of the record, the -- those check-points manned by young men were check-points off those two main roads.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I wonder, if Your Honours please, if the witness could be shown the public version of his 92 ter statement, that's Exhibit 271, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, I'm going to show you versions of -- copies of your statement; one is going to be public and one will be in private session. Could you please look at this version that I now produce to you on the -- on the screen? MR. DI FAZIO: And if the usher would -- if the court officer would be so kind as to scroll down and indicate the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that -- does your signature appear at the bottom of that document?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And it gives details of various dates of interview and places of interview, locations, and the persons who interviewed you in producing that statement. Are those details correct?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, as far as I can see, everything's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. And you've had an opportunity to read that statement that you provided to the various officers of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I read it before I signed it, and I read it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And does it provide information that you would provide if questioned about those various topics?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please and if there's no objection, I don't think I need to take him through each and every page with each and every signature. I would now like to tender that document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, Rule 92 ter (A)(iii) asks that a witness attest that a written statement of transcript accurately reflects that witness declaration and what the witness would say if examined. Now, you could say it's almost the same, but since the rule asks for both, I think you asked him the first one. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, would you give the same answers if examined on these matters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against admission? No objection. Then the 92 ter statement, we're now talking about the public version, that is Exhibit 271, is admitted into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Subject -- if I may respectfully say so, no objection subject to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the observation you made --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the objection that I made earlier on about the admissibility of certain conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That's understood, if Your Honours please. Thank you. And now I'd like to, if Your Honours please, move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, you've provided the parties and the Trial Chamber with a lot of information in your statement. I want to ask you, basically, questions about one major topic in your statement -- in the statement you originally provided to the OTP, and that concerns events that took place on the 11th of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, by the time the 11th of August, 1998, came about, how long approximately had you been in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Almost -- almost a month, a little bit less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And by this stage, had you travelled up and down the roads connecting the main towns, in particular Pec -- the roads connecting Pec, Decani, Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Almost every day, except the first three to four days that I spended to know the area, you know, even in -- in the town of Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And was one of your duties the observation of fighting that was occurring between Serb forces and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, on the 11th of August, did you go out on patrol, so to speak?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, we followed the schedule as every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how were you travelling on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We had our own armoured Land Rover, and we have a senior of European Union and monitors in both languages, in Serbian and Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did the vehicle that you were travelling in, the Land Rover, did it have decals or stickers attached to it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: All these flags that I mentioned and the insignia were stickers attached to the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. And what did the stickers and the insignia denote, what did they say, in other words?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It was the phrase, a single word "observations" -- excuse me. "Observers" in both languages, Serbian and Albanian. They had also big flags of European Union and two small flags of Greece --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you're answering your question, just sit a little bit closer if you don't mind to the speakers so we can pick up what you're saying? And incidentally, wait for me to finish the questions because it all has to be taken down and as it's not being interpreted on this occasion, the -- our conversation's going faster than normal.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to show you a photograph, please. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still do not know what the small flags were from. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said the two small flags of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of my country, the two small flags of Greece, it was one on the back and one on the front of the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. I'd like to show a photograph, please. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 65 ter 1334, please? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that a photograph of your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And the vehicles I think you can see -- the stickers I think you can see on the door of the vehicle. Is that the -- showing the European Commission?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please I seek --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: One matter. Underneath is a date, electronically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Di Fazio, you asked for private session at the beginning of the -- of showing the witness the non-public version of his statement but we did not return into open session. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, I'm sorry. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session and the Chamber hereby decides that that portion of the evidence, which was given after the confidential statement had been confirmed by the witness, will be public.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, I was just asking you about this photograph, now that we're back in public session. You said that that's the vehicle that you and your team used, and there's just one last aspect about the photograph that I want to ask you about and that's the date down below. Is that an accurate date or not?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, no, it's not accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's wrong with it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I -- I bought the camera earlier in Bosnia during my tour of mission, but it was bought from a Norwegian PXO. I couldn't read the instructions and use it properly. So, it's a little bit earlier than it should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I think the expression you used was a Norwegian --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- Norwegian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- Norwegian PX, and that's some sort of military store for soldiers on duty?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, right. That's it. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours, please, I'll tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P272, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection? No objections, admitted into evidence. Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber on the 11th of August, when you went out on your patrol, who exactly was with you on that occasion, who constituted your team?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The team at that day was myself, the gentleman Kaufmann, Wolfgang Kaufmann. There was a visitor from RC Belgrade, and his name was Penti and he was Finnish, as I recall. We also had an interpreter with us, and -- in any case, that we were driving outside of the road in KLA areas, we only had with us the Albanian interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Who was in charge of the team?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The man in charge was the German guy, Wolfgang Kaufmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned the visitor from RC Belgrade, is that short for Regional Centre Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, were you interested in observing fighting?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: As soon as we start driving southwards on the way to Decani from Pec, where we are located, we heard shell explosions very distantly, and we were trying to -- to go closer. That was our main purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What direction were you actually headed towards? What area were you interested in?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: As always, we were driving southwards on the way to Decani and further to Djakovica, and then we were leaving the road between Decani and Djakovica, and we were moving easterly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why did you leave the road? What was your reason in leaving the main road?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were aware that that was a main area for KLA presence in our area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why not use the main road to go south?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: At that occasion that we were able to hear shell explosions, Wolfgang, Mr. Kaufmann, decided to -- to take another road than the main one in order not to have any delays or stopping from Serbian check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Okay. So your -- do I understand your evidence to be this: You were interested in getting to a particular area?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Could you have, in an ideal situation, could you have got to that -- could you have gotten to that area using the main road if you had wanted to?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah. I believe that we could do that, but we might be a little delayed or --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was going to delay you? What was going to be a problem, if you had taken the main road?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Sometimes when the Serbs wanted -- wanted us not to see something, they were alleged -- they were alleging security reasons not to let us pass, but of course after some discussion, they were obliged to lead us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Well, do I understand that you left the main road because of fears that the Serbs may stop you at one -- at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And can you remember which road you took once you left the main road to get closer to -- well, wherever you wanted to go?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I can't recall each and every name from villages that we passed, but if I see a map ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to produce a map to you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit D32, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, I'm going to -- a map's going to come up on the screen in a moment.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of that screen that you have in front of you, just to the side - perhaps Mr. Usher might help here - is a magic pencil on which you can mark the route with a magic pen, so to speak, and you can just pick it up off the side of the screen and touch the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you, please, assist the witness? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And you can touch the glass on the screen and mark your -- the route that you took. So I'm going to ask you to do that, and before we get to that point, I'd like the map to be enhanced a bit. The -- it's the mid-left-hand quadrant that I'm interested in. That's probably --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: A little bit bigger, not so zoomed-in. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoom out. MR. DI FAZIO: -- zoom out a bit. Just -- no, that's too far.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that okay? Okay. Now, if you could just look at the map and mark with a pen the route that you took and indicate the names of the villages you passed through before your journey came to a halt on that day.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Given that we start from Pec, came southwards, we took the way to Rausic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: And from that point -- I have to have a little bit of a zoom here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a problem. As the witness starts marking, any change in zooming-in or zooming-out would -- I would then suggest that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I make a practical suggestion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've got some paper copies in A3 size, and if the witness at least has that in front of him, then he'll be in a position to see precisely what it is he's looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, would that help you, if you would have a paper copy next to you which you can consult when marking the electronic map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that would do better. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, marking, you're invited to do the marking on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So we -- we got off the road, the main road, in the place next to the village of Rausic. We'd been there, and then we follow this country road all the way to Krusevac -- MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you perhaps indicate that, please?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Krusevac, here, this way. And then we moved to -- to Brolic, which is on the south of Krusevac, maybe around here. And then we moved to Ljumbarda, Donja Luka, Pozar, and finally Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And have you marked all of those now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not yet, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ljumbarda, Donja Luka, Pozar, and Rznic. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Don't touch the screen again. MR. DI FAZIO: And, if Your Honours please, I seek to tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P273, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections, then it is admitted into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: And I'm grateful to the Defence for providing the hard copy of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about what you saw along this route. I'm not talking about what happened in Rznic, I'll get to that later, but first what you observed and saw along this route. Firstly, were there any check-points?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, we find some from Rausic and further. In some occasions we found some check-points, and there was a main one in Krusevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, what sort of check-points were these? Who manned these check-points?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: People in civilian clothes. They were not wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And were they members of any organisation?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I couldn't say that because when we were asking if they were KLA, without wearing a uniform, nobody was admitting that. They were saying that they were fighting, but no KLA members.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see -- all right, okay. Did you see any insignia on the clothes of these people?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: At that time, no, until there -- until Krusevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what happened in Krusevac?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: From that point and on, we were seeing people fleeing the area, you know, leaving the area, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'm just talking about check-points at the moment.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, until Rznic, we find no other check-point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Did you see civilians on -- as you took that trip to Rznic?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, we saw a lot from Krusevac almost until Kodralija, which is very close to Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just describe for the Trial Chamber what you observed, what sort of numbers, who these people were, how they were moving?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It's only a rough estimation, but I would say they might be 2.500, maybe 3.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And were they civilians and of Albanian ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how were they moving, were they travelling?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They were moving on -- on foot, and some of them on horse-carts or tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: At this time, as you are approaching Rznic, could you -- could you hear the sound of shelling?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes. On our way down there as -- as long as we were approaching Rznic, we were hearing louder and louder these explosions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So as you -- all right. So it -- were you, in effect, approaching an area that was being shelled?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you have any idea what that area was at the time, as you were heading down the road?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were just estimating that it would be from Rznic until Babaloc. This -- this area, it's about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you -- as you moved along the roads and saw the convoys, did you -- did you seek the services of a guide?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes. We were trying to find an elevation, a place that were not being problems of safety, and at the same time we would be able to -- to observe what is happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. And so that's what you wanted to do, so how did you achieve that?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: So for -- in Kodralija, that place close to Rznic, there was a young man that told us he can lead us to a place like that and Kaufmann invite him to -- to come to our car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where did he take you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He took us straight to Rznic, which is not in -- a place that you -- you could say that it's an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And did he leave you at Rznic, this young man?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you now about events in Rznic. Firstly, was there shelling occurring at the time and -- in the area of Rznic?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: There were shelling, but very close to Rznic, in Rznic also, but most of the shelling was south-east.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what happened once you arrived in Rznic.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Once we arrived in Rznic, the place was abandoned, there was no people there, nobody. So we stopped in a place that it should be the centre of the village, we stopped the car. We got down, we got off the car. We were trying to see if there's anybody in the close area. And at the time, myself and Penti tried to convince Kaufmann that it's too dangerous for us to be there, so he decided that we should leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did you make an attempt to leave?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, we got in the car. We turned the car on, tried to leave the place, and then there was a car from -- a small jeep, and two men were inside and they blocked our way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were these men in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, they were wearing kind of German uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say "German uniforms," were they camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I would rather say German-like uniforms because it's the same type of uniform that I -- I saw in Bosnia first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Was it a camouflage uniform, even though it may have been a German camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they have any insignia on -- on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They have insignia of UCK, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. You mean KLA?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And they were armed?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Okay. What did they -- what did they do? What did they ask of you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They stopped us, and they were asking what are we doing there, who are we, and these kind of questions. And they asked us to turn around the car again and be back to Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: While that -- whilst you were first dealing with these men, was there any shelling going on?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, there was and after we stopped at the same almost position that we stop in the first place, they ask us to follow them into a yard with big walls around. They were leading us into a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: And there was an explosion of a -- of a shell very close to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Maybe 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: I'd like the witness to look at two photographs. I can do these fairly quickly, if Your Honours please. They're 65 ter 1331, page 13 and 14 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, I'd just like you to have a look at these photographs and tell us if you recognise -- recognize them? MR. DI FAZIO: And if they could be shown one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thanks. Do you recognise that area?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What's that? What does it show?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Firstly, it's taken from the road that we approached Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It shows right in front the place that it was totally -- it was only grass there in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It is a big square. And then on the left hand, where you see the car parked --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- that's the place where we parked our car. In front of this, there's a big door of the yard of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And if the witness could just be quickly shown the other -- the other photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And I don't think there's any doubt, that's the same area, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, tender --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- these two photographs would be -- or do we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, it's not entirely clear to me. They are -- MR. DI FAZIO: They form --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- annexes B and C to the witness statement? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check. So there are three attachments, and many of the other documents the witness is talking about are not attached to the statement? MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's just -- MR. DI FAZIO: I may not actually need to tender this, since it's already part of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: If --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If this is part -- if these attachments are part of the statement, there's no need to further tender them. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well. Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you -- did you walk into Rznic with these two men, these two KLA soldiers or drive in towards Rznic?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, we were just -- entered the house when the shell exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: So they were maybe concerned about us, too, and they said to us, You are free to go -- go away, you know, and then we -- we enter again the car to leave the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Before you did that, did you see any damage? Were you shown any damage, any damage in Rznic?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Not at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. So you -- you decided to leave, and did you attempt to leave?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, we got out of this main gate, let's say, of the yard of the house, and then we saw another group of people, five, six persons, coming to us, and they were also KLA in uniforms, and they were a little bit upset.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Okay. And these were KLA -- men in uniform with -- armed and with KLA insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, same with the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I see. And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The -- they were enraged, let's say, and they were upset. They asked us to follow them, and they were showing us around places that were shelled recently, maybe the same day, like the mosque you see in the -- on the picture, on the right side of the picture, it was shelled. And very close to that was an unsophisticated field hospital also.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That was damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. And how long were you with them looking at this -- this damage?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: About 15 minutes. We were walking around in this place, and they were saying stuff in Albanian, and they were showing us around the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And your Albanian interpreter was providing you with an interpretation as to what was -- what was being said and the comments that they were making?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He was trying to do that, but, you know, they were talking a lot of people together, and he was giving us an overall what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Okay. And it's clear they're upset about the damage that had occurred to the village?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, that lasted about 15 minutes, did it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Almost, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. What did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They told us the same with the previous group of two men, to leave the place, and then we -- we got in the car almost, all of us, trying to get away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you manage to get away?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, because at the same time that we were trying to leave, another car arrived, it was a black jeep, black -- big one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how many men were in this black jeep?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Three men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, what sort of uniform did they have, if any?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They have different uniform. They had black uniforms with insignia of KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And were they armed?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, they had, two of them, guns in their hands and some waistcoats -- waistcoat with pockets for ammunition and stuff and knives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And what did they say -- what did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: For another time we had the same set of questions, you know, Who are you? Why are you here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what was their demeanour? By that I mean, what -- how did they -- how did they appear? What sort of mood were they in?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Well, they were much more aggressive than the ones we met before, but not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue your narrative. They -- you said that they were aggressive and they had some questions for you, and continue telling us what happened.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They were yelling and gesturing, especially the one that I -- I would say he was the man in charge. And after a very brief time of maybe one, two minutes, he ordered us to get into the car and follow his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, we did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Why did you do -- I'd like you to explain your thinking and the reasons why you did what you did to the Trial Chamber. Why did you follow and simply not turn your vehicle around and go in the opposite direction? What -- what was it that made you feel that you were compelled to do this?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Definitely --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's an extraordinarily leading question in the circumstances. The word "compelled" may well be one of the issues --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you rephrase your question? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll rephrase it. I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: My question is simply this: Why follow them?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The feeling was that it wouldn't be so wise not to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that your feeling or was that discussed amongst the men in the car, in the vehicle with you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It was discussed in the vehicle, and we also were very worried because we saw that we were moving to -- to the main area of shelling at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what area were you, in fact, moving towards?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were moving to Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you arrive there?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, we arrived about two, three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And where did you stop?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We stopped on a small road where there were houses around, big walls, like the one we saw in Rznic, and yards. One specific place were a lot of people coming in and out and we thought that was an HQ of KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you look, please, at 65 ter 1332? Do you recognise that place?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That's a place in front of which we stopped on that day, the one we thought it's the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And when -- on the day that you stopped there, was that rubble or stones, was that --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- visible?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- that was not the image that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do you know who took this photograph and when?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I took that photograph myself. It might be middle of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And why? Why did you take that photo?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were at the area patrolling again, and I recognised the big doors and that place, that specific place, that we had this incident and as a memory of mine I get the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. When you -- when you took this photo, was the -- were there buildings inside this -- inside this area or behind those walls?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: There was one that one can see next to the -- on the left side of the door. There is obviously a room inside this -- inside this door -- these walls, but there was another floor on the top of this, another storey.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So does this photograph show that other storey that you mention?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, it's completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And I don't think this photo is part of the 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, that's exactly what is so confusing. We have annex A, annex B, annex C, but usually if you make an annex to a statement or a document, in that document you find what annexes are attached. I don't see anywhere in the -- or perhaps I have not read carefully, but I do not see in the 92 ter statement any reference to any annexes. MR. DI FAZIO: To these particular annexes because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- because they were -- they arise as part of the statement that was removed from the -- from the 92 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's so confusing. So now we have annexes to a document which do not in any way say that they are annexes, and now it turns out that annex D is not part of it, and annex A, B, and C are. But we have seen earlier B and C, these are the photographs of the -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what was described by the witness as the centre of Rznic. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that an identity document related to this witness is annex A -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is attached, although not mentioned in the statement. And that now annex D is the photograph just shown which is not attached to the 92 ter statement. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that photograph would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P274, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any objection to its admission? I see no objection, so therefore it is admitted. At the same time, Mr. Di Fazio, let me just try to fully understand -- let me just ... MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, let me just try to understand. The witness took this photograph. Yes? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, therefore, it reflects what he saw at the time, I take it. MR. DI FAZIO: On -- a month later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon? MR. DI FAZIO: A month later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A month later. MR. DI FAZIO: Or thereabouts, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, middle of September -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that explains -- yes. Yes. I overlooked that. I apologise. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Might I just ask Mr. Di Fazio to explore, if possible, with the witness in as much detail as he's able to when exactly this photograph was taken in relation to visits to Gllogjan upcoming? MR. DI FAZIO: Sure, I can do that. I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if you are exploring that, I also wonder, Mr. Di Fazio, I don't know whether you wanted the Chamber to understand from the testimony of this witness who was responsible for the damage done by the shelling or not -- MR. DI FAZIO: If he can answer it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- I'll get full details on that, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, please, explore the matter. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: We've been talking about events thus far that occurred on the 11th of August?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that date, when did you take that photo that you can see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I believe it's same day that we visit with the rest of the team the place that bodies were found in a mass grave, and that's on the 18th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I see. Right. Of course, you refer to that in your statement, and that's the visit to the lake?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So when you conducted that visit, you think that's the day that you stopped in --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- Glodjane and took that particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that what your memory tells you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the other question that the Trial Chamber wanted answered, if you can, is the rubble that you see there and the damage -- or at least the rubble that you can see piled up against that wall, have you any idea who caused that and how it was caused?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you saw the place on the 11th of August, was that wall clean, so to speak, without any rubble on it at all?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, it was clean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Your Honour, I think that's about as far as the witness, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. So you've got to the point where you've told us that you followed the jeep, and you stopped at this location that you can see on the screen. Were there -- were there other people at this -- at this location, apart from the men who you'd followed and apart from your own group?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, there were a lot of people coming in and out from this --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What sort of people? How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Most of them, they have these camouflage uniforms that we said before, with insignia of KLA. Some of them, very few of them, were wearing black uniforms --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- except the men that took us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Well, it's not quite clear from what you say. The men that took you there, the men that you've already spoken about and you said that they were in black, dressed in black uniform?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Apart from those men whom you followed in the jeep, were there other men at this location dressed in black uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Only a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Only a few?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long were you at -- outside of this compound, this location?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Only a few minutes. Two, three minutes maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And can you please tell the Trial Chamber what happened when you were at this location, and this is the period of time when you first arrived, the first two or three minutes?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We stopped the car right after the black jeep, and then we were ordered to get out of the car. And when we all get out of the car, the man, as I said, in charge of these -- this group of three persons, he was very upset, swearing in Albanian and saying things. And he was calling us Serb spies.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how do you know he was calling you Serb spies? Did you understand what he was saying at the time or is that information you acquired later?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No. At the time, we could not say what he was saying to us. We could not understand that. After the whole incident, we found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that via your Albanian interpreter?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were the stickers still on your car?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: At the time, yes, but after few moments, after he was -- start shouting and gesturing, he was -- start getting off the stickers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And which one is "he"? Who do you refer to there?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I refer to the person that seemed to be the head of this group of three persons that took us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you describe the physical -- physical -- MR. DI FAZIO: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Pardon, Mr. Di Fazio, could you pause a little bit between answers and questions. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honours, it's -- I'm -- it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You know, for what purpose -- MR. DI FAZIO: I should be more mindful of it, and I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: It's my mistake, Mr. Pappas, I'm just going too fast, but bear in mind -- have some mercy on the interpreters who have to translate all of our -- all of our phrases. I'd like you to provide a physical description of the man you have described as the leader of this -- of this group of three. Can you give us an idea of colour of his hair, complexion, his height and his age, if you can?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah. I wrote back then a report, and to be exact I went through this report to remember all the incidents and all the persons I was describing. That report went to the Embassy of Greece in Belgrade and Sarajevo, and I was describing that person as of height of 1 metre and 70 centimetres; dark hair; and I would say a little bit dark complexity [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Slim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What we need to know, what the Trial Chamber needs to know, is whether you are in a position to provide a description of this individual from our own memory, or whether you have to rely on some report that you've -- you've provided in the past?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I could easily recognise the face because I don't forget easily, you know, faces. But for the overall description, I should check my documents, too. I mean, the age or -- it was about 20, 25 years old at the time. That was my estimation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Forgive me for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wonder whether Mr. Di Fazio can throw any light on the existence of such a document because, again it may be my mistake, but I'm not aware of having received copies of that particular report by this witness to the Greek government. I have another report by him to the Greek government, and I have a report filed with the ECMM, but I don't recall seeing the document that the witness has obviously consulted sufficiently recently to be able to refresh his memory on the descriptions that he's giving. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Emmerson is correct. The report that has been provided, which I provided to the Defence last week, is a report authored by this witness, and it concerns events essentially at the -- most of it concerns events and observations at the lake. There is a second report that the witness provided. Now, I haven't seen that report. I know that the witness has it and the witness -- could we perhaps go into private session just to complete the submission, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, another matter which can be dealt with also in open session. A correspondence has been copied to the Chamber in relation to Witness 60, and the Defence has indicated that this correspondence might have relevance for the proofing decision the Chamber will have to take. Under those circumstances, it would be appropriate - I'm not saying whether we are going to use it either in favour or not in favour of one of the parties, but then it would be appropriate to file this so that it's officially on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And at the same time, Mr. Di Fazio, then since it has been suggested that it's relevant material for our decision, if the Prosecution would respond to the relevance of this new development, you have an opportunity to do so. You know already the correspondence the Defence is expected to file, if you want us to look at it, within the next 24 hours, and the Prosecution has 36 hours to say something about it. It's just an incident to which our attention has been drawn, no more, no less. It's not really argument, it's just illustration, I would say, rather than anything else. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pappas, we have considered the matter, and we would like to instruct you, since you declared you were willing to do so, we would like to ask you, therefore, to make the redactions in the statement, at least in a copy of the statement, and provide the redacted statement to the Tribunal for translation, so that the parties can at least look at that. You're also invited to be as economic as possible in your redactions; that means redact only those portions which you really consider that should not come to the attention of others. That could be matters about individuals, telephone numbers, strategical considerations as far as safety is concerned. What the Chamber after that will do with the remainder of the document, we have not decided that yet, whether we will invite you to give the whole unredacted document to the Chamber or perhaps to the Prosecutor to find out -- on a confidential basis, in order to find out whether there's anything in there which would be exculpatory for the accused, because under those circumstances it might be considered unfair not to inform the Defence about exculpatory elements which are in the remainder of the document. We have not decided that yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider it, but you at least are already invited at this moment to, with a black marker, to already make the redacted statement, and again the less you take out, the bigger the chances that the Defence will be quite happy with it. So therefore, it might avoid future litigation if you are not overcautious. Just be as cautious as need be.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I also would like to instruct you that you should not dispose of the original of the document -- I mean, the original, the full document. So you're supposed not to tear that into pieces or to lose it or to burn it. Just keep it, and the Chamber will then further consider what to do with the document in its entirety. But we gladly accept your offer to start with receiving a redacted statement. Is that clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Di Fazio, you may -- MR. DI FAZIO: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: We were at the point where I was asking you to provide a description of the man that you said was the leader of the group of three or the one you perceived to be the leader of the group of three. And you made reference to another -- another matter. Forgetting -- just relying on your memory, just on your memory alone, are you in a position to give the Trial Chamber a physical description of the man that you -- you saw as the leader?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell the Trial Chamber what that was?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Before the witness does so, perhaps it would be appropriate to explore with him whether he has, indeed, refreshed his memory by reference to that document prior to coming into the court and whether that has assisted him in recalling the description that he is about to give. He has already been asked this question, has already given the answer to it in point of fact, but the point that interests me and concerns me is whether or not that is a recollection based on 1998 or whether it's based on sometime earlier today having reviewed a document he wrote in 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pappas, would you please in your answer specify to what extent your answer is based on your memory of what you still remember to have seen at the time and to what extent your answer is based on recent review of your reports on the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only figure that I -- I would say remembered going through that document that I refer is the height because at the time we were standing one close to the other, so I could figure out what was the height. But when it comes from face figures or general figures like hair or whatever, I would recollect that easily without any report. I remember everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say, therefore, that the length of the person, that's something you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- took from your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- from your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas, the other elements --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The other elements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you still remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I still remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Well, don't tell us about the height of the person, but tell us about the other features that you say you remember, the physical features of the person you describe as the leader?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He was slim, as described, and athletic stature, dark hair, dark complexity, same with the eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You mean dark complexion?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Complexion, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: And same with the eyes. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. How long were you at the -- were you at the front of the house before leaving that area and moving in?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It was only a matter of minutes, let's say two, three minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And during that time were you able to see this person you've described as the leader of the group during that course of that -- those two or three minutes?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, he was the one who ordered us to step off the car, to get off the car, and then he was -- I suppose he was swearing -- I'm not sure because we could not have translation at the time, and he was taking off the stickers from the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during that time that you -- between your arrival at the house and going elsewhere, did anything happen to the interpreter who was with you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes. After he removed the -- the man in charge, let's say, he removed the stickers from the car, he started beating and kicking the interpreter, calling him names, and making some gestures like he was trying to get the gun from his waistcoat and shoot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was he using his fists?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were any members of your party, namely Mr. Kaufmann or Penti or yourself, able to provide any assistance?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Not at the time, but then we were ordered to get into the house, to the yard of the house, where he continuously was hitting and kicking and punching the interpreter. The same thing with gestures and then Kaufmann was closer than the rest of us were, and he -- he tried to move towards the interpreter to protect him. But then we heard the -- some of the guys around there cocking the guns and we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. You've said that there was soldiers or men in uniform at this -- at this location.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And you've mentioned being inside the yard of this -- this house. Whilst you're inside the yard of the house, did you have an opportunity to see other people there, apart -- other soldiers, apart from the group of three that had picked you up in -- in the jeep?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, there were a lot of people in there. Some of them were very young. I -- I remember that there were three, four persons like 13 to 16 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And how long would you say that you were in the yard for before leaving it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were about five, ten minutes, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So about three minutes outside, or thereabouts, outside of the house when you first arrived, and about five to ten minutes inside the yard?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And during that period of time, was the one that you've described as the leader of the group of three present?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Following -- where did you move after you -- after the yard?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were ordered to - how do I say? - to follow the stairs to the upper floor of what we saw before of this building, small building. As I told you, there was a storey more, and we were ordered to -- to step off -- or step on the stairs and get on the other floor. It was a small room there with some benches, some wooden benches, and a chair, and we were ordered to be in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So who was inside this room when you were first taken into the room? Just go through the names, please.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It was Penti, the Finnish guy; it was Kaufmann, the one from Germany; it was myself -- me; and also the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And apart from that group, were there any other men in the -- in the room?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, they left a person in black uniform to be a guardian of ours in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, could I still insist on a short pause between question and answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry. Yes. Thank you. I'm grateful to you for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Were you able to speak with the guard, or did anyone speak to the guard, or did the guard speak to you, to the group?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were trying to figure out what is happening, you know, asking interpreter, but he was not in a position to -- to answer or to have any discussion, long discussion. He just said that we were in their eyes like spies or something. And then he translated us that the guard said, We expect the chief to be there, so they will know what to do with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And did anyone -- did the chief arrive?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, after some minutes, from the time we had this translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: How long were you in the room before -- before that individual turned up?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We might be about a quarter before we have this translation from interpreter, and ten minutes afterwards, the man that we expected arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And I'd like you now, please, to provide us with a description of this -- this man referred to as the chief, his stature, what he looked like, and clothing that he had on.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No dispute that the man who came into the room was Ramush Haradinaj. MR. DI FAZIO: All right. There we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then there's no need to pursue this matter. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful for that. It will save some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: So what did Mr. Haradinaj do?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He was trying to find out, like the ones before, who are we, what are we doing there, but it was totally different, the way he was asking information or the way he was behaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And in what respect? What do you -- you say it was totally different, what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: You know, he was polite and he start speaking in English that we all could understand. And everything he done in there, it was quite civilised now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he speak to all of your party?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He spoke to each one of us separately, starting with Penti, and he asked him to -- to sign in a blank paper so he could see the signature from his passport.
