And then he asked him something about the lake in dispute with Russians in Finland, so he could say possibly if he's really Finnish or what.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I see. That's what you concluded? You thought that was the reason --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, that's personal conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right, okay. Yes, please continue. And what other questions did he ask the individuals in the room?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, then he talked with the Albanian interpreter, but it was all conversation in Albanian, and even after this incident the interpreter didn't tell us what he said. And after one, two minutes this lasted, the conversation with Albanian interpreter, he asked me who I am, what I do in Greece? I ask him -- I answer him sincerely, and I explain him why we were there, how we found ourselves in Rznic, what are we doing in Kosovo in general, asking him to be more, let's say, cautioned with us because we were in an area under shelling, and we were there to report what's happening, not -- not anything else we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he appear to accept that?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, he was quite open and understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the interrogation or the questions, I should say, come to an end, and did you then leave the room?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No. He -- he started talking with Kaufmann, both in English and French, and he was asking same questions like the rest of us, where is he from, what is he doing? That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. What happened after all of that concluded?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: After the, let's say, interrogation finished, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He asked us if we have any guns on us, you know, or in the car. We said we don't carry guns. This is a mission without armoured personnel. And then he escort us in the car -- to the car outside of the yard. He -- he made a small inspection of the car himself, opened the doors, checked inside, and after two, three minutes, he said that we can go, and he asked if we would want some escort to show us the way out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During that time that you were back at your vehicle outside of the -- of the premises, did any other soldiers appear?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, there were two cars stopped right when we -- when we passed the door of this yard, stepping outside of the house. There was about -- there were about eight persons in the cars, these two cars, among them a woman. They saluted. They stepped off the car, they saluted Haradinaj with a fist on the forehead. And then he said something, and they got into the cars and directed to the front line, where the shooting, you know, was coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And was an escort provided to you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, it was the same three persons that leaded us there with the same jeep. They drove us back to, as I can remember, just a minute, to Kodralija, I think, and then we took our way back ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did the three men who escorted you, the men who had originally taken you to Rznic, did they -- was it their idea to escort you or were they told to?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, no, it was an order from Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. So you -- you made it to Ljumbarda, you think, and -- sorry, Kodralija?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Kodralija.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what -- what you did there?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: When we -- when we were escorted there, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please. What -- who --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The black jeep, you know, turned around and continued his way, and we took our way back on -- on the same path that we arrived at this area, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you speak to anyone in that village?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah. When we were very close to -- to Kodralija, I don't recall now the name, the name of the place, we find the guy that he was originally in Rznic when I said that five, six men appeared and they gave us a tour, showing us the damage of shelling. There was a guy there that he -- he knew already what happened to us, that we were detained, and he ask us if we want to -- to follow him in a close-by hospital they had. We've been there and we had this small discussion with five, six persons in a small room. It was a friendly discussion, no -- in a quiet place. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What was the discussion about?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: About what happened to us, you know, and they were asking -- they were -- apologise about this incident. And after some minutes, we had the -- started this discussion, another man came in, about 50 years old, and he -- they stood up, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just interrupt you there? You've been describing what "they" did.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who exactly are "they," if you wouldn't mind telling us?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: The men that I mentioned before, the three men with black uniforms, that they led us to temporarily detainment, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And the other man that came in who was about 50 years -- 50 years old and they all stood up, who was that person, as far as you could ascertain?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I didn't know at the time his name. I don't know it since now, but he introduced himself with a nickname Toni, Commander Toni.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did he have KLA uniform and insignia?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He had --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Or at least KLA insignia --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He had the camouflage uniform, and he had the KLA insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He -- he was told what happened to us in front of us from the rest of the KLA members, and he said he was very sorry that this thing happened but there are extremistic groups inside KLA that were operating in their own manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, can -- let's try to keep it -- MR. DI FAZIO: As slow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- a bit slower. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, in recent times, were you contacted by your superiors concerning testifying in this case?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question you posed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: All right. Have you ever looked at the ICTY web site?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What I'd like you to do is to explain to the Trial Chamber how it was that you came to do that and the reasons why you did that?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I -- I received about a year or so paper -- a report from my General Staff headquarters of Hellenic Force, and they were informing that I had been asked to testify for a specific case in ICTY concerning -- I saw three names in that paper, but I didn't know who they were, you know, at the time. So in order to inform myself -- yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I question the relevance of this line of questioning. I think I know where it's going, and if it is to be going in the direction of anything approaching what would be close to a dock identification, it is something that I think ought to stop right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey -- Mr. Di Fazio, you're now supposed to answer on the basis of what is just a supposition and assumption. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. If we might have this conversation, I know that the witness does speak English. If we might have this conversation in the absence of the witness because I think there are a number of issues that might arise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, there are some procedural issues at this moment which the parties would like to discuss without bothering you with it, and therefore I'm asked to invite you to leave the courtroom for a second so that we can speak about it without it having any influence on you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio -- yes, Mr. Guy-Smith, it was just your suggestion to have the witness leave the courtroom. Mr. Di Fazio, perhaps you first tell Mr. Harvey whether you are slowly getting at a dock identification or not, or ... MR. DI FAZIO: No, not in the sense of classic dock identification from these particular accused in this dock. I think Your Honours know that -- perhaps you don't. But the evidence I intend adduce is this: I expect the witness will say that he looked at the -- as a result of being told of his intended testimony, he looked at the ICTY web site and looked up the details of this particular case and saw photographs of the accused in this case, printed off the pages, and recognised the other two men whom he has spoken about in his evidence as being Mr. Balaj and Mr. Brahimaj, and of course Mr. Haradinaj, but that's not an issue of course. And he says that having seen those photographs he recognised Mr. Balaj as the man he has referred to as the leader of the group and Mr. Brahimaj as another man who was standing in the yard at the time that he was taken into the yard. And that's the evidence that we intend to adduce.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Oh, my prophetic soul. That's what I thought we were going. I have a number of problems with this. First of all, as I said, this is as close to a dock identification this makes really no difference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The dock was just on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And it is therefore, in my submission, worthless as evidence. The second issue that I have, and this puts me in the rather awkward position of testifying, is that at early stages in this case, my client's photograph didn't even appear on the web. There were two photographs of Mr. Balaj, one alongside Mr. Balaj's name and one alongside Mr. Brahimaj's name. I have no means of knowing what the state of the web site was at the time that this witness viewed it and whether, indeed, it was Mr. Brahimaj's face that was even on the web site at that time. I don't think any of us can ever know that with certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from the web master, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Apart from the web master. I -- Mr. Emmerson thinks that I may be taking a bad point here and that perhaps my client's photograph was available to him at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I wasn't implying that at all. I think that the witness in one of his witness statements when he deals with this claims that he still has the photographs that he printed off the internet so if it needs to be investigated, then it could be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: It's pretty much a subsidiary point, though, and I stay with the first one primarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's -- if it's any assistance to Your Honours, my, as Your Honour knows, my client's case is that identification is not in dispute, but my client's case is that the identification of Mr. Brahimaj is in error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to hear that that's my case as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine it is. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- I might need to be heard on this, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You know that usually if you -- if you get up on your feet, then usually I allow you to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Indeed so. Thank you so much. It is our case that the identification of my client at the time and place is not inaccurate but the characterisation may well be. Meaning that he was there, but the activities attributed to the individual who was the leader of the group are not him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So it, mainly as far as identification is concerned of Mr. Brahimaj rather than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct and I will be revisiting the issue of length of a person once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is aware that this has some similarity with a dock identification; there are differences, however, as well. The witness is, I take it at least, not asked, Mr. Di Fazio, to say do you happen to see someone here in the courtroom who was there at the time, but is rather asked about at what moment he has become aware that what he saw on -- and I do not know to what extent he had identified in full detail what the case was about, et cetera. Therefore, the Chamber will consider the evidence to be given with great care and very cautiously. Of course, the evidence also may give an opportunity to -- for further test of the reliability. And in view of the issue you raised, Mr. Harvey, whether at all at that time there were any photographs, which of course would then be a reliability issue. Certainly the Chamber would like the parties to deal with it, whether Mr. Di Fazio already asked the witness whether he still has kept these photographs and whether you do it in cross-examination is open. If neither of you will do it, the Chamber will do it. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Obviously, it's not my direct concern on this, but since it raises issues of identification and dock identification, Your Honours will recall that the stated position of the Prosecution in these proceedings is that they will not seek dock identification, and the only caveat to that that's ever been entered is that they may reserve the right to argue that where the identification is not of someone seen on a single occasion but of someone known well over time, they may reserve the right to make a further argument in relation to it. And I simply make the observation that the witness's statement in relation to Mr. Brahimaj is unable to ascribe any role to him or to indicate where it was he said that he was involved. It's a momentary sighting, according to the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey, the concerns you expressed are well understood and have not led to a ruling that Mr. Di Fazio could not put questions in relation to what the witness saw on the internet. Apart from that, it's perhaps also good for us to know whether he had other sources which, whatever the witness will testify about it, the Chamber will have to consider as a potential source of further information. Mr. Di Fazio, we'll invite the witness to come into the courtroom again, and you then may continue. And I take it that you have carefully listened also to the matters raised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Pappas. Mr. Di Fazio will continue his examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: We got to the point where you said that you looked at the ICTY web site. Just explain once again to the Trial Chamber why it was that you looked at it.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I saw an official paper, you know, the case IT-0 -- something, which tells me nothing and of course some names on it, which again they were not ring a bell, you know. So I wondered why -- why should I testify for a case of these persons if I don't know them. And I tried to -- to have some information about them, about the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That's why I entered the web site of ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you put a time on this? Do you recall when it was that you accessed this web site?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It might be late of April, early of May --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Was that the first time you had accessed the ICTY web site?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you access it subsequently?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, just that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Having accessed the ICT web site, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: At the beginning, I was a little bit confused. I didn't know what to search, you know, and I went to this engine -- search engine you have, I put the number of case, and then I read the allegations, I would say. I saw that -- that paragraph concerning the mass grave that was found in Lake Radonjic, and I thought to myself: That's the case. And then I saw pictures, you know, of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And -- thank you. Thank you. And did you print anything off from the web site?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, I print -- I printed three pieces concerning each one of -- of these pieces concerning each one of the accused, it was a picture of them, and the general allegations they were facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you keep the pictures of the three accused?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, I kept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you bring them here?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, it was in my papers that I have gathered together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And when was that? When did you bring them here, here to The Hague, I mean?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: On the 2nd of May, when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'd like you to look at -- sorry, one more question. And did you provide those pictures to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at this --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I do find this quite extraordinary. Apparently, these pictures have been provided to the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And not disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: -- and once again not to the Defence. Unless I have missed something, and if I have, I will certainly apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: But I look around me at my fellow counsel, and I see also shaking heads and disbelief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Di Fazio is -- seems to disagree and will explain why. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: My firm understanding is that the statement, the full statement, of the witness has been disclosed with all of the annexes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2006, 2007 -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yeah, the full -- the full, and -- and the 92 ter. Of course it was disclosed, unless something has gone horribly wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I must say that -- MR. DI FAZIO: And it's referred to in the body of the statement as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Um, well, there is -- MR. DI FAZIO: It's extraordinary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- some confusion about annexes to the 2007 statement. Now, the issue is -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said on the -- "the 2nd of May, when I arrived." Now, it happens that both in 2006 and 2007, the interviews were in May. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. I've just double-checked. I've just conferred with my colleague. They were supplied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They were supplied.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: They were supplied to me. I have them. I don't know whether or not Mr. Harvey has them. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes -- MR. DI FAZIO: -- it was my firm, clear understanding that they had been disclosed. Of course, they were absolutely crucial. How could I have overlooked it? If they haven't, then it's the result of some completely unforeseen error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I remember from this over this weekend that -- first of all, I earlier expressed -- is it in -- is it attached to the 2007 statement or the 2006 statement? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. And I've got a letter here dated -- sorry, an e-mail dated 10th of May, 2007, sent at 8.35 p.m. "Dear Defence counsel and Mr. Zahar, witnesses for next week and so on," and lists for Mr. Pappas the various documents -- various exhibits, including two-page internet extract showing the faces of the three accused with an ERN -- ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not without a microphone. That's impossible. Now it's -- it's on.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's it. No, just to say my impression was that I had not received them either, but they have been found in our system also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: With a slightly red face, I confess that I have finally found mine as well. It is hard to keep track of these, but thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I do apologise for -- MR. DI FAZIO: No apology needed at all. It's -- if they hadn't been sent, it would have been a matter of grave concern to everyone, but I was pretty confident that they had been sent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I'd like you, please, to look at the Exhibit 1333, which I think is a two-page document. Now, is that -- is that the -- one of the pages that you printed off?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And it had all the personal details of these men at the time you read it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: What you see here, that's the only thing I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And can the witness be shown the next page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And are these the two pages that you provided to the Prosecution when you recently arrived at The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, these are not attachments, although still confusing -- MR. DI FAZIO: They --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- attachment A, B, and C are attached to the 2007 statement, although they originate from the 2006 and were earlier attached to that one. But now I do understand that this D and what we have now E, I think, are separate documents. Madam Registrar, that would be two pages and together would that be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P275, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection at this moment? It just shows what the witness at that time saw, and that's now on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With what the Chamber's just said, there's no objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: With that caveat, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- then P275 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Could we go back to the beginning -- to the first of these two pages, please? And could we have them -- yes, thanks, just perhaps a bit more, if we can. Thanks. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, the -- the gentleman depicted in the top photograph, it's -- that's not in dispute, we know that's Mr. Haradinaj. And the gentleman depicted in the photograph at the bottom, in the context of what you saw and observed on the 11th of August, 1998, who is that individual?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That was the man --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think he's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think Mr. Di Fazio is -- is -- is going at it in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think as a matter of fact, Mr. Di Fazio, you're now heading for a dock identification, the dock being on the screen. You are -- you can ask the witness when he saw these pictures, what -- what came into his mind at that moment? MR. DI FAZIO: I'll paraphrase Your Honour's -- Your Honour's questions exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you looked at the -- the web site and you saw the photographs, and in particular the photographs of this individual at the bottom, what came into your mind?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I instantly recognised the man who hit the interpreter, and he was the man, he was leading the team of three.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Who led you from --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That led us --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- Rznic to Glodjane?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: And could we now turn to the second page?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Same question: When you opened the ICT web site and saw that particular photograph, what came into your mind?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He looked familiar because I saw him in the yard of this house, but he didn't participate to any beating or detention of our team.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: You had no -- no dealings with this man?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Other than his presence in the yard?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, have they been -- that's been tendered. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Pappas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's already admitted. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you. If Your Honours please, I wonder when you propose to take the break --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact -- yes? MR. DI FAZIO: I'd like to move on to the issue of some documents and it's -- I really need an opportunity to speak to the Defence about this, and I wonder if now would be an appropriate moment to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it certainly would be an appropriate moment. We have a break until five minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours for taking the break at that time. It's hopefully helped us to deal with the next part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Mr. Pappas, in your 92 ter statement, you have referred to a visit to -- you made to the canal area or the Lake Radonjic area, I should say. I'd just like to show you very briefly, very, very briefly a couple of video-clips and a photo and ask you to tell us -- provide us with some comments? MR. DI FAZIO: Now, can the witness be shown this excerpt from P72.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And just look at the screen, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole is already in evidence? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The whole of it is? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Just an excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Now, follow it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just pausing there momentarily, do you recognise -- it's difficult to see, I know, but do you recognise that location?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, it's the location we've been 18th of September or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Is that the -- a canal leading into Lake Radonjic?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It's the concrete canal, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice any features on the walls, any marks on the walls during your trip to the canal, the sides of the walls that you can see there depicted in the video excerpt?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes, we saw a lot of marks on the wall. We've been told that it's bullet marks. I'm not an expert to say, but I saw a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Just continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you see marks similar to those that you can see on that particular part of the excerpt?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And who informed you that they were bullet-holes?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: With us, with the Team Pec I at that day that we visited the site, it was the head of -- I don't know how to say that, head of prosecutors, head of judges --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: [Indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- this district, yes. It was -- his name was Cvejic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: He was giving us explanations there what they find and where.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And he was a Serbian?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: A Serbian court official; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please -- thank you. Your Honours, I think that's already in evidence, so there's no problem there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, it's always good to know exactly what has been shown to the witness. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's approximately from - I didn't notice immediately - but from 8 minutes 10 seconds up until 8 minutes and 50 seconds. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm grateful to Your Honour for noting that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, just one more question. The bullet-holes that you -- that you -- I think you can see in the excerpt that you have just been --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio, those have yet to be established. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith is quite right, and I'm grateful to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: These holes that you were told were bullet -- bullet-holes that you saw, were they on both sides of the wall of the canal; in other words, some inside or -- and on the outside?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: It was only at the outside part of that wall, and when it comes to the other wall, the opposite, which these two walls are limit the canal, there were bullets on the other side, too. But not both sides of the same wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. But I -- what I'd like --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's one thing for a witness to be invited to give evidence of a positive, but if the witness is going to be invited to -- or to give evidence of a negative, we're going to need to establish that he inspected the entire length of both sets of walls, because the testimony he's given is not consistent with the photographic evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry, would Your Honour just give me a moment? I'm only trying to adduce evidence of what the witness -- whether the witness saw these sorts of holes on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Di Fazio, the witness said -- and that's part of his evidence and I take it that Mr. Emmerson would very much like this to be explored properly, whether or not it has not been specifically asked about it, I think. Well, yes, to some extent he was. He said: "But not on both sides of the same wall," which - and that's from what I understand from Mr. Emmerson - means that he has looked as carefully to the one side of the wall as to the other side, in order to be able to draw such a conclusion that there were no bullet-holes at the other side of the wall or even at the other sides of the two walls. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Yes, well, I'm -- I won't ask any further questions about that. I'd like to -- to show the witness another excerpt, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I'm -- what I'm asking for is for the foundation to be laid for the assertion that there are bullet-holes on one side only of each of the walls, if that is the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You've invited Mr. Di Fazio to do that. If no foundation has been laid, then there's just the assertion, isn't it? Yes. Mr. Di Fazio, of course that limits the relevance and the probative value of the evidence. I take it that you're aware of that? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. Would Your Honours just give me a moment to confer with my colleague, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you inspect the inside of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Only from the one side that we approached the canal, not from the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And where were you when you did that, can you recall? What part of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That could be from the west side of the canal where the bodies were found, the main area the bodies were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When you say the area where -- "the west side of the canal ... the area where the body -- the bodies were found," you -- you didn't actually see any bodies, of course?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: No. So you rely there on what you were told by the Serbian officials; correct?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you conducted that inspection, as you say, from the west side of the canal, did you see holes that were said to you to be bullet-holes on the inside of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, not at this part of the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you conduct or did you inspect other parts of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just look at this particular excerpt?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Firstly, do you recognise that particular part -- that particular -- what you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And what is it?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: That's another set of marks on the wall which was at the opposite side of the canal, as we were looking at the time that I visit there. We been -- said, again, that there were bullet marks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Do -- you may not know, but did you actually see those particular bullet-holes, or is your testimony that you saw bullet-holes like that on the inside of the canal?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: I've got to be clear so that we all know. Are you saying that you can't remember if you saw these -- this specific part of the canal with these specific bullet-holes?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: I stepped on that concrete wall to see down there, and I don't recall to see any marks from the inside of that wall. But it was only at this specific place. I didn't examine other places around.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Was it that place that you can see in the video-clip that you saw these holes?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the record, it's at 7 minutes, 28 seconds, that's where the picture appears. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. And finally can the -- on this topic, can the witness be shown Exhibit P45.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Witness, have a look at that particular photograph carefully. Do you recognise it or do you know what that depicts?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes. I might say I recognise the place because it was just before the concrete canal finishes, you know, and there was a natural creek from that place on. So I can say that I recognise the place, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd just like you, if you would, please, to use that red marking device on the side of the computer. Could you show, indicate, on that the -- any area that is visible on that photograph that you went to on the day that you went to the lake area?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were just visiting that place here, where we show the bullet-proof -- or the bullet marks, or what it's supposed to be bullet marks. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to any other places along that canal and natural creek or gully --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- that you can see depicted?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We've been to a farm, but I'm not sure if that's the one on the top. We were heading east, south-east from direction of this concrete wall, and I think that's the one because I remember it was about 1, 1 and a half kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. But as far as the canal area is concerned, is that the only area of the canal that you visited, that you have shown with a circle?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: At that day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you perhaps just write your initials on the circle showing the point at which you viewed the canal, perhaps AP?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Where I viewed the canal, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, just put the initials next to that so we know what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. And so the other circle that is unmarked -- sorry, that has no initials, that's the -- the place that you think is the farm that you also visited on the same day?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number P276, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Please proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Usher, I have no further need to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: During the course of your duties, did you -- did your team cause or prepare reports from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: If our team preparing reports --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Yes, Team Pec I.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We are supposed to give report every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And to whom?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We had a kind of hierarchy that -- if you take it from the bottom, we were all teams, Pec I, II, some teams from Mitrovica, some other from Pristina, subordinated to a coordination centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. Where was the coordination centre located?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: In Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber the -- on a daily basis how the report-making was conducted and what would occur?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We were having some scheduled meetings, but this was coming -- this was happening when it comes to Serb authorities because they were known, they had telephone numbers, you know, to contact. We had regular meetings and we had interviews. We were asking anything we wanted, keeping notes. And then we had also patrols, and every day we were creating a summary of what we'd done every day and till 3.00 we are supposed to send our report to CC.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Right. When you say till 3.00, do you mean you had to send your report at some point prior to 3.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You used an abbreviation, you sent the reports to CC?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: You said to the coordination centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And in your particular team, Team Pec I, who wrote the reports or did that vary from time to time?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: For -- on behalf of two teams, Pec I and II, most of the times German Kaufmann would do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you ever participate in the report writing or help by providing information to him?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes. I participate a lot of times, but the final draft was issued by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Once the report had been prepared, what was the next step?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: We have -- we had an -- our private network to send the reports by computer, and then coordination centre was gathering all reports of the day from all teams in Kosovo and creating -- and they created a summary, a brief report, consisting of main items from each team. And they were sending it to RC Belgrade, which is regional centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And are you aware if other teams, such as your own, were conducting the same exercise throughout Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: They were conducting the same exercise, you mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Conducting -- other teams, like yours, doing the same thing --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- throughout Kosovo? All right. Preparing a daily report --

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Every day, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: -- sending it to the coordination centre?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: And from there, the coordination centre sent it to the regional centre?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever have an opportunity to see reports that the coordination centre was forwarding on to the regional centre?

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: Only unofficially, you know, when I was visiting CC Pristina and some of our colleagues were writing down, the operations officer were -- was writing down a report --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ACHILLEAS PAPPAS.
utterances.text: -- and if I was close to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I want to deal with some specific documents now, and it's necessary to do that in -- in private session, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I invite you, Mr. Pappas, that as soon as you've done it, to give it immediately to the Victims and Witnesses Section, who will then, because you're supposed not to meet with the Prosecution anymore, will then pass it to the registry so that the registry will take care that it will be translated. Final question: How many pages is the document, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I remember, it's about four or five pages tops. I'm not sure, but I think it's four.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the part that will remain would be approximately --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would be the same --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you determine --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- except some phrases or some small part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
